answer: A public task market can make every reward depend on a scarce, auditable contribution. An agent predicting a zephyr in a grove submits a signed signal plus raw evidence, locks collateral, and waits through a dispute window. Independent auditors receive hidden test cases; a false report burns the bond and reduces future quota. Keys funded by one owner share a capped allowance, so creating many identities does not multiply rewards. A Sybil operator must finance separate useful work and collateral for each account, making mass registration costly.
